definitions.explanation: A large mammal with one or two humps on its back, adapted to desert conditions. Used for transportation and carrying goods.

examples.japanese: ⟦{砂漠|さばく}→砂漠：09508_sabaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{駱駝|らくだ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}りました→乗る：00511_noru⟧。
examples.english: I rode a camel in the desert.

examples.japanese: {駱駝|らくだ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦なし→無し：03779_nashi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{長|なが}く→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦{生|い}きられます→生きる：01184_ikiru⟧。
examples.english: Camels can survive for a long time without water.

examples.japanese: {駱駝|らくだ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{瘤|こぶ}→瘤：noentry⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{脂肪|しぼう}→脂肪：03199_shibou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{蓄|たくわ}えられています→蓄える：08996_takuwaeru⟧。
examples.english: Fat is stored in the camel's hump.

examples.japanese: {駱駝|らくだ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{砂漠|さばく}→砂漠：09508_sabaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{暑|あつ}さ→暑さ：12973_atsusa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{寒|さむ}さ→寒さ：12336_samusa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: Camels are animals that can withstand both the heat and cold of the desert.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{商人|しょうにん}→商人：03236_shounin⟧⟦たち→達：01551_tachi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{駱駝|らくだ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{荷物|にもつ}→荷物：00737_nimotsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{載|の}せて→載せる：28290_noseru⟧⟦{砂漠|さばく}→砂漠：09508_sabaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}り→渡る：02441_wataru⟧、⟦シルクロード→シルクロード：noentry⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{通|とお}って→通る：01243_tooru⟧⟦{東|ひがし}→東：02250_higashi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{西|にし}→西：00659_nishi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国々|くにぐに}→国々：04806_kuniguni⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{結|むす}んでいた→結ぶ：02308_musubu⟧。
examples.english: Merchants of old loaded their goods onto camels and crossed the desert, connecting the countries of East and West through the Silk Road.

notes:
The kanji {駱駝|らくだ} is rarely used in ordinary writing; the katakana form ラクダ is standard in newspapers, textbooks, and zoo signage, and hiragana らくだ is also common.

TYPES:
- ⟦{一瘤駱駝|ひとこぶらくだ}→一瘤駱駝：noentry⟧ - dromedary (one hump), of Arabia and North Africa
- ⟦{二瘤駱駝|ふたこぶらくだ}→二瘤駱駝：noentry⟧ - Bactrian camel (two humps), of Central Asia

COLLOCATIONS:
- {駱駝|らくだ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧ - to ride a camel
- {駱駝|らくだ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{瘤|こぶ}→瘤：noentry⟧ - a camel's hump
- {駱駝|らくだ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{荷物|にもつ}→荷物：00737_nimotsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{運|はこ}ばせる→運ぶ：01088_hakobu⟧ - to have camels carry the load

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{馬|うま}→馬：01865_uma⟧ - the riding and pack animal familiar in Japan; {駱駝|らくだ} fills the same role in desert regions
- ⟦{家畜|かちく}→家畜：06431_kachiku⟧ - livestock, the category {駱駝|らくだ} belongs to in its home regions

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
Camels are not native to Japan, so most Japanese meet them at a ⟦{動物園|どうぶつえん}→動物園：01686_doubutsuen⟧ or on the tourist rides at the Tottori sand dunes. In writing they appear mostly in connection with deserts and the Silk Road. Written in hiragana, らくだ is also an older word for warm knitted underwear, originally made of camel wool.

COUNTER:
Counted with ⟦{頭|とう}→頭：18067_tou⟧, the counter for large animals.
